description: Composite of three SEM fractographs of tensile-failed specimens, one panel per alloy, each carrying a yellow-bordered low-magnification inset of one half of the broken specimen. (a) 28Mn0Ni: fully dimpled ductile surface with deep equiaxed microvoids of mixed size separated by fibrous tearing ridges; its inset (1 mm scale bar) shows a cup-and-cone fracture with a rough central fibrous zone and shear lips. (b) 28Mn5Ni: a comparable dimple field, somewhat finer and flatter, again fibrous with microvoid coalescence; the inset also shows cup-and-cone geometry. (c) 15Mn5Ni: markedly different — a nearly flat macroscale surface (inset shows no cup-and-cone, only a flat, radiating-marked face) covered by numerous micro-cleavage facets and flat platelets connected by shallow dimples. All three main micrographs carry a 10 µm scale bar; panel labels (a)/(b)/(c) are printed in the corners inside small boxes; insets carry 1 mm scale bars. No numeric values other than the scale bars. Overall the group demonstrates that 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni fail by ductile microvoid coalescence, whereas 15Mn5Ni fails by crack-initiation-controlled quasi-cleavage with facets linked by dimples.
measured_quantities: scale bar length in main fractographs (µm): 10 µm
scale bar length in low-magnification specimen insets (mm): 1 mm

observations.observation: Panel (a) fractograph shows a fully dimpled ductile surface with deep equiaxed microvoids separated by fibrous tearing ridges, with a 10 µm scale bar printed bottom-right.
The inset in (a) is a low-magnification SEM image of one half of the failed specimen with a 1 mm scale bar, displaying a cup-and-cone fracture with a rough central fibrous zone.
Panel (b) shows a dimpled, fibrous fracture surface similar in character to (a) but with somewhat finer and shallower dimples, evidencing microvoid coalescence; 10 µm scale bar at bottom-right.
Panel (c) shows a much flatter fracture surface dominated by angular micro-cleavage facets and flat platelets interconnected by dimple ridges, in contrast to (a) and (b).
The inset in (c), 1 mm scale bar, shows an almost flat fracture face without cup-and-cone necking, unlike the insets of (a) and (b).

The figure consists of three fractographs labelled (a), (b) and (c) corresponding to the 28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni alloys tested in tension, with insets showing low-magnification SEM images of one half of each tensile specimen after failure.

The caption states that both 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni alloys exhibit clear cup-and-cone type failure, evident from the dimples, suggesting ductile failure involving microvoid formation, growth and coalescence.

The citing text states that the 15Mn5Ni alloy specimen displayed numerous micro-cleavage facets connected by dimples on a nearly flat surface at the macroscale (Fig. 6c), indicating crack-initiation-controlled fracture triggered by the B2 stringers.
The citing text relates the distinct 15Mn5Ni fracture surface to its lower strain-hardening exponent n (Fig. 5b) compared with the 28Mn(0,5)Ni alloys, giving different ductility levels.
The citing text attributes cleavage facets in the 15Mn5Ni fracture surface to the B2 phase, connected by dimple morphology, and states this is consistent with Park et al. [23].

subfigures.description: SEM fractograph of 28Mn0Ni tensile specimen, 10 µm scale bar: deep, rounded dimples of varied diameter with well-developed tearing ridges and fibrous walls between them. Inset (yellow border, 1 mm scale bar) shows one half of the failed specimen with a cup-and-cone shape: rough central fibrous zone surrounded by slanted shear lip.

SEM fractograph of 28Mn5Ni tensile specimen, 10 µm scale bar: dimpled, fibrous surface similar to (a) but with somewhat smaller and shallower dimples and flatter regions between them; microvoid coalescence still visible. Inset (1 mm scale bar) shows cup-and-cone failure geometry of the halved specimen with a fibrous central zone.

SEM fractograph of 15Mn5Ni tensile specimen, 10 µm scale bar: strikingly flatter topography dominated by angular micro-cleavage facets and flat platelets bridged by shallow dimple ridges. Inset (1 mm scale bar) shows an almost flat fracture face with radiating/chevron-like markings and no cup-and-cone necking.
